st.headline: ‘Not about certification for certification’s sake’: What HR credentials can offer firms and workers
st.teaser: Larger organisations in Singapore must have at least one IHRP-certified HR professional by July 1, 2028.
fullText: SINGAPORE – After spending more than 20 years in operations and industry development, Wilson Tan moved into a regional human resource role at his company, Stolz Engineering, in 2024.
The senior manager of people, culture and organisational capability described the transition as one that left him with “a quiet dose of impostor syndrome”.
He said ga ining certificat ion from the Institute for Human Resource Professionals (IHRP) helped him bring more structure to work he had previously approached through operational instinct.
He said his employer gave him the flexibility to study alongside carrying out his regional responsibilities and apply what he learnt at work.

When handling workplace changes, Tan now uses IHRP’s Body of Competencies as a guide. This national competency framework defines the skills, knowledge, and mindsets HR professionals need to deliver strong employee experiences and sustainable business value.

During the roll-out of a company-wide enterprise resources planning system and career conversion programmes, he said he listened to employees’ concerns and explained how the changes could reduce repetitive work and support their growth.
“I learnt to step back, see challenges through an objective lens and ‘think like a marketer’ by actively selling the ‘why’ to secure genuine buy-in rather than forcing compliance.”
By July 1, 2028, organisations with more than 200 employees prepare must have at least one suitable HR professional certified at IHRP Certified Professional level or higher.
An equivalent qualification may also be accepted, subject to IHRP’s bridging requirements.

The requirement covers about 2,000 organisations, including 300 with at least 1,000 employees and 40 with at least 5,000, according to an earlier parliamentary reply by Acting Manpower Minister Jasmin Lau.
Together, the organisations employ more than 45% of Singapore’s total workforce. About 45% already have at least one IHRP-certified HR professional.
Lau also said the 200-employee threshold was chosen as a practical starting point, focusing on companies with the scale and means to take the lead on certification.
IHRP has seen more e-mail enquiries and participation in certification application clinics since the requirements was announced in September, its chief executive Aslam Sardar said.

He added that the certification requirement is a minimum baseline and encouraged employers to develop capabilities across their HR teams. The number of professionals a company should certify would depend on its size, business needs and workforce complexity, he said.

IHRP encourages employers to identify candidates early and offers preparation materials and assessment tutorials. Training partners, including the Singapore National Employers Federation (SNEF) also run preparatory programmes.

SNEF chief executive Hao Shuo said employers should set aside time for candidates to prepare, particularly to refresh their knowledge of Singapore’s labour laws. Some companies may need to balance preparation with manpower constraints and operational demands, he said.
Eligible Singapore citizens and permanent residents can receive a one-time $100 subsidy between Oct 1 and June 30, 2028, bringing the IHRP-CP certification fee to $163.50, inclusive of GST.
Eligible candidates can also use SkillsFuture Credit, while employers will be able to tap a redesigned SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit, with further details to be announced.
The certification is valid for three years.
The July 2028 deadline gives employers time to prepare, said a Ministry of Manpower spokesperson, who encouraged them to start early and make use of available support.

Carol Yap, director of HR and administration at Safran Aerosystems Services Asia, believes certification gives her company assurance that its HR professionals have the knowledge and competencies to fulfil roles effectively.

Certified as an IHRP senior professional, she said her biggest hurdle was taking the first step to register for certification. “Having spent more than 20 years in the HR profession, I found myself questioning whether I really needed another certification.”

She added: “I don’t think obtaining the certification necessarily changes the way I practise HR. After all, the experience and knowledge gained over more than 20 years in the profession have shaped the way I approach HR matters today.”

Nonetheless, revisiting HR case studies allowed her to refresh and reinforce her understanding of HR practices and employment legislation, she said, adding that the preparation journey was “a valuable learning experience”.

NTUC assistant secretary-general Patrick Tay stressed that the 2028 requirement does not require every HR professional to be certified, “so individuals should not feel pressured to pursue certification regardless of their circumstances”.
“Ultimately, this is not about certification for certification’s sake,” Tay said.

“It is about strengthening HR capabilities so that companies are better equipped to make fair and responsible workforce decisions, and workers can have greater confidence in how these decisions are made”.

cna.headline: China stocks surge most in two years as Beijing vows stronger market support
cna.teaser: China’s benchmark stock indexes jumped about 4 per cent, posting their biggest daily gains in more than two years after Beijing signalled stronger support for the market.
fullText: SHANGHAI: China's share benchmarks jumped 4 per cent and the yuan rose on Friday (Nov 27), after Premier Li Qiang chaired a State Council meeting that called for a bigger role by "national team" investors to stabilise a falling stock market .

Chinese stocks have struggled this year despite policy easing, reflecting investor concerns over weak domestic demand, a prolonged property downturn and uncertainty over the economic outlook hurt by trade wars and geopolitics.

The benchmark Shanghai Composite Index ended 4.2 per cent up and the blue-chip CSI300 index was 3.7 per cent higher at the close, both notching their biggest daily gains since October 2024 when China rolled out massive stimulus measures to revive the market.
China's tech-focused STAR 50 Index surged 15 per cent, the biggest one-day jump in two years.

In Beijing's strongest gesture yet to support a stock market that had fallen to 16-month lows, the Cabinet said "capital markets were crucial to the broader economy", state media Xinhua reported. The Cabinet added that Central Huijin - the domestic unit of sovereign wealth fund China Investment Corp - would enhance its role as a quasi-stabilisation fund to ensure ample liquidity.
The meeting also called for better policies to encourage long-term funds to invest in the stock market, and for measures to strengthen defences against risks spilling over from overseas markets.
"It's a shot in the arm for markets," said Kenny Ng, a strategist at Everbright Securities International in Hong Kong.

"Sentiment has been downbeat for so long. There hasn't been much good news to trade on. At least now there's something to count on: the national team will come to the rescue if things really turn south."
The Chinese yuan gained 0.1 per cent against the dollar in offshore trading, reversing earlier weakness to hit its strongest in three weeks. The currency is nearing its firmest level in four years.

"It's very rare that Executive meeting of the State Council would make such direct comments. Last time it happened was 2024 when they rolled out a liquidity support package," said Jason Chan, a Hong Kong-based strategest at Bank of East Asia.
Given the current low investor expectations, any incremental supportive policies would help boost confidence, said Meng Lei, China equity strategist at UBS Securities.
The latest statement follows the margin lending relaxation and trading fee reductions announced over the weekend, underscoring the government's growing determination to stabilise markets.
LSEG data showed trading volume surged across broad-based benchmarks and sub-indices after the midday break, pointing to a sharp improvement in investor sentiment.
The CSI Semiconductor Industry Index and the STAR Chip Index both shot up more than 17 per cent.
Indices tracking China's AI, cloud computing and consumer electronics stocks jumped more than 10 per cent.
But some analysts said it was too early to suggest the market was near a bottom as support from the national team alone was unlikely to lead to a sustained rally.
"There is an increasingly clear signal that Chinese authorities are uncomfortable with the extent of the equity market selloff," said Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo Bank.

"I would distinguish between a turning point in policy resolve and a turning point in market fundamentals... A policy-induced bounce needs to evolve into a fundamentally driven recovery before we can confidently call it a durable bottom."

Also on Friday, Xinhua Finance reported that regulators will launch a campaign to further tighten rules on share sales by controlling shareholders of listed companies. Regulators will also guard against listings by "pseudo-tech" companies, or firms that inflate earnings, the state media said.

economistArticle.title: The fall of China’s most trusted wealth manager
paras: For over a decade, CreditEase stood as a glittering symbol of China’s private wealth boom, connecting affluent entrepreneurs with high-yielding shadow-banking products. Established during an era of double-digit economic expansion, the firm successfully positioned itself as a dependable intermediary for individuals seeking alternatives to low-yielding bank deposits.

However, the unraveling of China's property sector gradually eroded the foundation of this financial juggernaut. As real estate developers defaulted on their debt obligations, the underlying assets backing many of CreditEase’s flagship wealth management products rapidly deteriorated. Investors who had grown accustomed to reliable double-digit returns were suddenly confronted with delayed payments and restructuring notices.

Regulatory scrutiny further exacerbated the firm's predicament. Beijing's decisive campaign to dismantle toxic shadow-banking channels forced wealth managers to bring off-balance-sheet items back into full public view. Under strict new regulatory standards, opaque financial structures could no longer mask non-performing assets, revealing systemic vulnerabilities that had long lingered beneath the surface.

The sharp downfall of CreditEase underscores a broader paradigm shift across China's wealth management industry. Individual investors are now recalibrating their expectations, shifting away from implicit government guarantees toward risk-conscious asset allocation. The era of easy returns derived from real estate speculation has unequivocally drawn to a close.
economistArticle.cn:
十多年来，宜信（CreditEase）一直是中国私人财富繁荣的耀眼象征，将富裕的企业家与高收益的影子银行产品联系在一起。该公司建立于两位数经济增长的时代，成功将自己定位为一个值得信赖的中介机构，服务于寻找替代低收益银行存款的个人人群。
然而，中国房地产业的崩溃逐步侵蚀了这一金融巨头的基础。随着房地产开发商违约债务，支撑宜信许多旗舰理财产品的底层资产迅速恶化。那些习惯了稳定两位数回报的投资者，突然面临延期兑付和重组通知。
监管审查进一步加剧了该公司的困境。北京方面拆除有毒影子银行渠道的决断行动，迫表外项目重新回到公众视野中。在严格的新监管标准下，不透明的金融结构再也无法掩盖不良资产，揭示了长期潜伏在表面之下的系统性脆弱性。
宜信的猝然倒下凸显了中国财富管理行业更广泛的范式转变。散户投资者如今正在重新调整预期，从依赖隐性政府担保转向具备风险意识的资产配置。源于房地产投机的轻松获利时代已明确宣告结束。

gems.s: Under strict new regulatory standards, opaque financial structures could no longer mask non-performing assets, revealing systemic vulnerabilities that had long lingered beneath the surface.
gems.why: This sentence employs cause-and-effect reasoning with strong imagery like 'mask' and 'lingered beneath the surface' to concisely capture regulatory impact. 这句话巧妙结合了因果句式与‘掩盖’、‘潜伏于表面之下’等生动动词，极为精准地总结了新规对于隐蔽风险的暴露力。
